instrument.state: An internal structure cannot be sampled directly, but variations within it systematically alter the propagation of signals that cross it along many paths.
instrument.operation: Measure signal travel behavior across many source-to-receiver paths, compare those observations with predictions from a candidate internal model, and iteratively adjust the model to reduce the discrepancies.
instrument.signal: The observed propagation times or waveforms differ from model predictions in spatially structured ways across the sampled paths.
instrument.inference: The pattern of discrepancies constrains a spatial model of internal properties that could have produced the observed propagation behavior.
instrument.limit: Sparse or uneven path coverage, measurement error, uncertain source locations, regularization choices, model assumptions, and non-uniqueness can create artifacts or allow multiple internal structures to fit the observations.

mapping.state: Unknown service-delay changes affect travel times on overlapping checkout routes.
mapping.operation: Measure old/new low-load endpoint times on r1-r3. Predict differences from candidate service-delay maps, iteratively adjust them to reduce route residuals and retain the non-unique solution set. Follow up on held-out r4 at old/new low load, checking predicted residuals rather than choosing a preferred internal map.
mapping.signal: Measured route differences and held-out residuals constrain compatible internal delay-change combinations.
mapping.inference: Localize deployment-associated delay contributions under the shared additive replay model and direct later service inspection; this is a bounded contribution to attribution, not proof of a code mechanism.
mapping.limit: Sparse paths, non-uniqueness, model error and measurement limits remain. Do not substitute hidden component truth for measured constraints or generalize beyond replay.
